candidate.answerReason: The increase of $5.06 equals December's usage charge. Subtracting it from December's $12.48 bill leaves the fixed fee of $7.42.

methods.label: Use the difference between the bills
methods.explanation:
January had twice December's connect time, so its connect-time charge was twice December's charge. The fixed fee was the same in both months. Consequently, the increase in the bill equals one December-sized connect-time charge:
\[
17.54-12.48=5.06\text{ dollars}.
\]
December's bill consisted of that usage charge plus the fixed fee. Subtracting the usage charge gives
\[
12.48-5.06=7.42\text{ dollars}.
\]
The fixed monthly fee is \(\boxed{\$7.42}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Comparing the two bills isolates the usage charge using doubling and decimal subtraction; no system of equations is needed.
